4892.title: [CI] Merge Arcade release infrastructure into 4.151.2
4892.body:
[CI] Merge Arcade release infrastructure into 4.151.2 (#4892)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4863
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/commit/01db053da47ba92241170895bc948c8cd483d139
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4871
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/commit/017438e18ca269f89b19887c75f8669a37b1d04c
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4835
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/commit/bbf7e97d631140855d9d8eda00dac5f1ba793939
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1572562
Changes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/compare/bbf7e97d631140855d9d8eda00dac5f1ba793939...e407e230dd3f8e66b6344c59e412b3861f7ace26

SkiaSharp 4.151.2 was cut but never published; NuGet.org's stable 4.151 line
still ends at 4.151.1. Its branch was therefore stranded on the legacy split
pipelines while the Arcade and dnceng release path was proven one line over on
release/4.151.x by #4863 and its #4871 bootstrap. Merge the exact source tip
01db053d into the exact 4.151.2 base bbf7e97d with a real two-parent merge, so
the point release becomes buildable through that path without rewriting or
losing either branch's ancestry.

Keep 4.151.2's identity instead of inheriting the source branch's post-release
bump. `scripts/VERSIONS.txt` stays at 4.151.2 and HarfBuzzSharp 14.2.1.102
rather than 4.151.3 and 14.2.1.103; HarfBuzzSharp must stay in the M151 bucket
because 14.2.1.2 is already published from M150 (#4835). Alongside it,
`scripts/azure-templates-variables.yml` keeps `SKIASHARP_VERSION: 4.151.2` and
`PREVIEW_LABEL: stable`, so an ordinary internal build of this branch emits
exact 4.151.2 packages. Those two files, plus the SetBuildVariables
expectations that assert their values, are the only difference from the source
tip.

Against 4.151.2 the merge is 207 files, dominated by the generated eng/common
Arcade snapshot and repository pipeline templates. It changes no managed API,
C API, native source, Skia submodule, or product behavior, and adds no package
IDs. It does replace this line's CI contract wholesale, described below.
Public Build 1572562 succeeded on 01db053d as
`4.151.3-preview.0.26428.3+4.151.x`, which validates the topology but not the
`stable` path this branch selects: no stable SkiaSharp has yet been produced
through Arcade, and NuGet.org publication remains a separate protected action.

~~ Arcade and Darc bootstrap ~~

The point release lacked the generated Arcade foundation the release flow
requires. Import #4871's pinned Microsoft.DotNet.Arcade.Sdk 11.0.0-beta.26414.2
metadata and its complete eng/common snapshot, loaded through an isolated
NoBuild restore graph so Arcade does not displace SkiaSharp's existing
Cake/MSBuild product build. Treat `eng/**` as a global cache input so
engineering changes invalidate product caches; the snapshot stays an
upstream-owned unit while future Darc updates remain repository-owned and
reproducible.

~~ Connected dnceng topology and execution policy ~~

The legacy Native, Package, and Tests definitions exchanged independently
numbered artifacts, obscuring which source produced the packages under test.
Make one Build own Prepare, Native, and Package, and connect Tests through the
folder-qualified `\dotnet\skiasharp\skiasharp-package` resource so downstream
runs inherit the producer's identity. Public validation uses the same stage
templates through the local 1ES output adapter, but signing, API Scan, and
publishing expand only in trusted internal non-PR builds. The historical
native-only and complete entry points are retained because this line still
consumes them.

The internal root depended on DevDiv templates that cannot resolve in dnceng.
Move it to the released 1ES Official template, drop that dependency, and make
Armory, BinSkim, CredScan, ESLint, PoliCheck, and PSScriptAnalyzer break the
build; keep network isolation in Audit until permanent mirrors and allowlisting
are ready. Always build and merge the MSVC Win32 artifacts: the old
`System.TeamProject == 'devdiv'` condition can never match here and would strip
the `native_msvc` input API Scan requires.

~~ Exact 4.151.2 build identity ~~

Loosely parsed counters and feature labels could assign different identities to
producing and consuming runs. Derive package build numbers from Arcade's
`yyyyMMdd.revision` OfficialBuildId, normalize GitHub and Azure Repos source
identity, and make connected Tests inherit the Build run name. Require exact
Build run IDs and reject mutable `latestFromBranch` selection.

PR builds use `pr.<number>`, scheduled builds use `nightly`, and ordinary builds
keep their configured label. Only an internal `release/*` producer may use the
`stable` sentinel, which clears the suffix and sets
`DOTNET_FINAL_VERSION_KIND=release`; anywhere else it fails closed. Malformed
or incomplete identities fail rather than manufacturing a plausible version.
The focused suite exercises PRs from both source providers, downstream
inheritance, exact 4.151.2 releases, and malformed input.

~~ One package and transport family ~~

The historical graph packed stable and preview products separately, then
created stable, preview, symbol, branch, and commit transport variants. Pack one
coherent product family per run and create one PR transport family for PR
validation or one branch transport family otherwise; omitting commit aliases
prevents BAR from receiving multiple versions of the same transport package ID.

This changes the artifact contract for consumers of this branch: `nuget_preview`
and `nuget_symbols` are gone, and `arcade_shipping`, `arcade_nonshipping`, and
`PdbArtifacts` are published beside the raw `nuget` and `nuget_special`
artifacts. Normal and transport packing now run in one job. Mark `_NuGets`,
`_NativeAssets`, and `_Dependencies` non-shipping with the metadata Arcade
requires, and make documentation and generated samples consume the one family
the build produced.

~~ Real loose PDB artifacts ~~

Arcade V3 requires PdbArtifacts, but cloning product packages into synthetic
fallback symbol packages would create false package identities. Preserve real
explicit symbol packages in Shipping; for product packages without one, extract
implementation and runtime PDBs under their original package, version, TFM, and
RID paths. Exclude `ref/**`, avoid duplicates when an explicit symbol package
owns the symbols, reject archive entries that escape the package root, and emit
`.empty` only when no eligible PDB exists. The package gate covers both
transport families, explicit-symbol ownership, reference exclusion, empty
output, and traversal rejection.

~~ Explicit signing and BAR inputs ~~

Arcade's broad defaults do not describe SkiaSharp's mixed first-party, Mac
developer, JavaScript, WebGPU, and transport payloads. Replace them with an
explicit repository policy: sign Shipping NuGets and classified first-party
contents, preserve Mac developer signing, and retain source payload bytes
through `CertificateName=None`. Keep NonShipping transport packages unsigned and
out of recursive SignCheck, with `DO-NOT-SIGN` exclusions making unexpected
signatures fail validation. Do not add the absent `SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET`
package or Apple symbol production to this historical line.

Generate one Arcade V3 manifest from signed Shipping and prepared NonShipping
assets. Release branches select real signing and BAR registration, while public
and PR template expansion cannot acquire those side effects. Keep
`publishAssetsImmediately: false` and require default channels before
promotion; BAR registration is not NuGet.org publication.

~~ Fail-closed API Scan coverage ~~

The legacy inline scan extracted packages without proving that required
binaries, PDBs, surrogates, or configured targets existed. Add a
repository-owned stage that consumes the current `nuget` and `native_msvc`
artifacts, activates the dedicated WIF identity, runs API Scan in release mode,
and breaks at Note severity. Prepare checked Win32, NanoServer, and WinUI
mappings, using x64 MSVC surrogates for Win32 and HarfBuzzSharp ARM64 targets
and staged x64 package binaries for WinUI ARM64 targets. Reject missing
packages, binaries, PDBs, surrogate files, or target matches, and run the
preparation suite during Prepare so drift fails before the protected stage.

~~ Historical toolchain and servicing-pool compatibility ~~

The branch's 10.0.108 SDK is too old for Arcade package download, while its
Apple and WinUI jobs cannot adopt every newer tool. Move repository-owned builds
and existing checkout-consuming native containers to SDK 10.0.203 with
`latestPatch` roll-forward, and retain workload set 10.0.202 for the macOS 15
and Xcode 26.3 combination. Visual Studio MSBuild 17.x cannot load a 10.0.2xx
SDK, so install 10.0.108 side by side for the WinUI and WinUI ANGLE jobs. Update
only containers present on 4.151.x.

Windows and Linux jobs move to the public or internal dnceng pools, which select
servicing images for `release/*` while retaining queue-time overrides and hosted
Apple jobs. The lean servicing Linux image lacks assumptions the former pools
hid, so provision the Android SDK, platform tools, build-tools 35.0.0 and
36.0.0, and configured API levels, pass `AndroidSdkDirectory` into Cake, and
install a SHA-256-verified pinned Chrome for both Linux WASM jobs. Separately,
point the nested tracking benchmark's `nuget.config` at the dnceng EAP feed;
it still restored from the legacy Xamarin feed and failed before
BenchmarkDotNet could run.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <maleib@microsoft.com>
Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

4863.title: [CI] Backport Arcade release infrastructure to 4.151.x
4863.body:
[CI] Backport Arcade release infrastructure to 4.151.x (#4863)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4802
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/commit/46ea7244b6ab7e021432dda16451c93e5c7a1117
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4842
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/commit/398bcdd123d907dbb7920a76c8d3ab5c8d7a034d
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4803
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/commit/2dd508790e44e115467bf38fb543ab69eebb4584
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4846
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4877
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/commit/6386960c2a4fddf0e68a8815856cbb7470deefce
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4859
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4889
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4883
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1571474
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/32862258889
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/33122720179

Complete the 4.151.x release line's move from its legacy split pipelines to
repository-owned dnceng pipelines and a standard Arcade V3 package flow. Keep
public validation free of protected side effects while giving trusted internal
release builds the signing, API Scan, BAR registration, and promotion inputs
needed to produce 4.151.3.

Preserve the branch's product, runtime, managed API, C API, native source, Skia
submodule, preview-workload, Xcode, and test topology. Do not add the Apple
symbol production from #4846, `SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET`, new product or
container families, generated bindings or documentation, or unrelated release
automation. #4859 supplied historical compatibility constraints, but its
manual release-skill design is superseded by #4889 and is not backported.
This change does not register, promote, publish, or otherwise release the PR
build.

~~ Connected dnceng release topology ~~

The old Native, Package, and Tests definitions exchanged independently numbered
artifacts, which obscured source, package, and test provenance. Make the package
root use `buildPipelineType: 'build'` so one Build owns Prepare, Native, and
Package, and make the connected Tests definition consume the folder-qualified
`\dotnet\skiasharp\skiasharp-package` resource.

Use the same repository stage templates in public validation through the local
1ES output adapter. Expand signing, API Scan, and publishing stages only for
non-PR builds in the internal project, so public and PR template expansion
cannot acquire protected release side effects. Retain the branch's native-only
pipeline role rather than importing the newer main-only topology wholesale.

Trigger the Build directly for `main` and `release/*` path changes instead of
waiting for a separate Native pipeline to finish. Keep the branch's
`azure-pipelines-complete-internal.yml` and native-only root compatible with the
shared stages because other historical entry points still consume them.

~~ dnceng execution policy ~~

The internal root still extended the DevDiv MicroBuild 1ES template and loaded
shared stages from `DevDiv/Xamarin.yaml-templates`, neither of which is
available to a dnceng-owned pipeline. Move it to the released
`v1/1ES.Official.PipelineTemplate.yml` and remove that repository dependency.

Configure Armory, BinSkim, CredScan, ESLint, PoliCheck, and PSScriptAnalyzer to
break the build, and run CodeQL on non-default branches. Keep network isolation
in Audit while permanent mirrors and allowlisting are completed; the policy is
intentionally not presented as fully enforced.

Build and merge the MSVC Win32 artifacts without the old
`System.TeamProject == 'devdiv'` condition. That predicate cannot match in
dnceng, and retaining it would remove the `native_msvc` input required by API
Scan.

~~ Exact 4.151.3 build identity ~~

Feature names and loosely parsed downstream counters could assign different
identities to producing and consuming runs. Derive the product build number
from Arcade's `yyyyMMdd.revision` OfficialBuildId, normalize GitHub and Azure
Repos source identity, and make Tests inherit the Build run name.

PR builds use `pr.<number>`, schedules use `nightly`, and ordinary builds keep
their configured preview label. Only an internal `release/*` producer may use
the `stable` sentinel to clear the suffix and emit exact 4.151.3 packages.
Emit `DOTNET_FINAL_VERSION_KIND=release` for that case and reject malformed or
incomplete source identities instead of manufacturing a plausible version.

Require exact Build run IDs when downloading pipeline artifacts and reject the
mutable `latestFromBranch` mode. Shared package downloaders use the branch
transport alias and no longer fall back to a commit alias, matching the one
transport version registered for each package ID. Keep this historical branch
fail-closed on its existing downloader shape rather than taking the broader
dead-code removal still under review in #4883.

The Prepare gate exercises GitHub and Azure Repos PRs, downstream run-name
inheritance, exact releases, and malformed identities. Build 1571474 used the
resulting `4.151.3-pr.4863.26427.5` identity.

~~ One package and transport family ~~

The historical graph packed stable and preview products separately and then
created stable, preview, symbol, branch, and commit transport variants. Pack one
coherent product family and create one PR transport family for PR validation or
one branch transport family otherwise. Keep commit aliases out of NonShipping
so BAR cannot receive multiple versions of the same transport package ID.

Run normal and transport packing in one `package_windows` job. Publish the raw
`nuget` and `nuget_special` artifacts beside deterministic
`arcade_shipping`, `arcade_nonshipping`, and `PdbArtifacts` views. Remove the
separate `nuget_preview` and `nuget_symbols` pipeline artifacts. Mark transport
projects non-shipping and give `_NuGets`, `_NativeAssets`, and `_Dependencies`
the Microsoft copyright, MIT expression, and project URL required by Arcade.

Documentation and generated sample jobs now select the build's single package
family instead of assuming stable and preview packages coexist. Package jobs
no longer restore from the shared build cache because package versions and the
transport family depend on run identity rather than repository inputs alone.
Shared consumers resolve transport packages from the dnceng transport feed.

~~ Real loose PDB artifacts ~~

Arcade V3 requires a `PdbArtifacts` input, but cloning customer packages into
manufactured fallback symbol packages would create false package identities.
Keep existing explicit symbol packages in Shipping. For product packages
without one, extract implementation and runtime PDBs under their original
package, version, TFM, and RID paths.

Skip `ref/**`, reject archive entries that escape the package extraction root,
and avoid loose-PDB duplication when an explicit symbol package owns the
symbols. Emit `.empty` only when no eligible PDB exists. A Package-stage gate
exercises both transport families, explicit-symbol ownership,
reference-symbol exclusion, empty output, and traversal rejection.

Build 1571474 published byte-identical raw and prepared package sets and a
path-safe `PdbArtifacts` payload containing only the intended loose PDBs.

~~ Explicit signing and BAR inputs ~~

Arcade's broad signing defaults do not describe SkiaSharp's mixed first-party,
Mac developer, generated JavaScript, WebGPU, and transport payloads. Replace
them with an explicit repository policy. Sign Shipping NuGets and their
classified first-party contents, preserve Mac developer signing, and classify
source payloads that must retain their existing bytes as `CertificateName=None`.

Keep NonShipping transport packages unsigned and prevent SignCheck from
unpacking them. `DO-NOT-SIGN` exclusions make validation fail if a transport or
listed source payload is unexpectedly signed. Do not add
`SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET` to the policy because that package is absent from
4.151.x, and do not manufacture or consume the Apple symbol packages added by
#4846.

Retain the source contract's `scripts/infra/signing` cache-input category even
though no such helper directory exists yet, so the cache configuration stays
aligned with main without importing additional tooling.

Generate the Arcade V3 manifest from signed Shipping and prepared NonShipping
assets. Main and release branches select real signing and BAR publication;
other trusted branches test-sign unless explicitly forced, and forced BAR side
effects additionally require `registerInBar`. Post-build validation keeps
`publishAssetsImmediately: false` and requires default channels before
promotion.

~~ Fail-closed API Scan coverage ~~

The legacy inline scan extracted packages without proving that its binaries,
PDBs, surrogates, or configured targets existed. Add a repository-owned stage
that downloads the current `nuget` and `native_msvc` artifacts, activates the
dedicated WIF identity, runs API Scan in release mode, and reports at Note
severity.

Prepare checked Win32, NanoServer, and WinUI mappings. Use x64 MSVC surrogates
for Win32 and HarfBuzzSharp ARM64 targets, and staged x64 package binaries for
WinUI ARM64 targets. Fail when packages, binaries, PDBs, surrogate files, or
target matches are absent, and make PostAnalysis fail at Note severity. Run the
focused preparation suite during Prepare so input drift fails before a
protected scan stage is requested.

~~ Historical SDK and pipeline compatibility ~~

The repository's 10.0.108 SDK was too old for Arcade package download, while
the branch's Apple and WinUI jobs could not simply adopt every newer tool.
Move repository-owned builds and the existing checkout-consuming native
containers to SDK 10.0.203 with `latestPatch` roll-forward. Pin workload set
10.0.202 for the branch's macOS 15 and Xcode 26.3 combination.

Visual Studio MSBuild 17.x cannot load the 10.0.2xx SDK used by Cake and managed
builds. Install the retained 10.0.108 SDK side by side for the WinUI and WinUI
ANGLE jobs. Update only Dockerfiles already present and consumed on 4.151.x;
do not import absent container families or main's later product and toolchain
changes.

~~ Servicing-pool runtime prerequisites ~~

The branch still used Microsoft-hosted and `Maui-1ESPT` defaults, so it did not
inherit Arcade's release-aware dnceng routing. Move the Windows and Linux
defaults to `DncEngPublicBuildPool` or `DncEngInternalBuildPool`, which select
servicing pools for `release/*`, while retaining queue-time object overrides
and hosted Apple jobs.

The lean public servicing Linux image exposed two assumptions hidden by the
general pool. Managed Linux builds Android libraries but did not install the
Android SDK because the bootstrapper installed it only on non-Linux agents.
Provision the SDK, platform tools, build-tools 35.0.0 and 36.0.0, and configured
API levels for every Android-installing agent, then pass
`AndroidSdkDirectory` into Cake.

Both Linux WASM jobs also assumed Chrome was preinstalled. Download the pinned
Chrome package, verify its SHA-256, package name, version, and architecture,
install it, and export `CHROME_PATH` before running product tests.

Build 1571474 completed the public release topology on the final head,
including managed Android and the WASM product-test paths. The artifact and test
outputs demonstrated that the servicing images now provide the tools these
branch-native jobs require.

~~ Tracking benchmark feed compatibility ~~

The nightly resolver selects versions from the dnceng EAP feed, but the nested
tracking benchmark configuration still restored from the legacy Xamarin feed.
The nightly benchmark paths in run 32862258889 therefore failed package restore
before BenchmarkDotNet could run. Align the nested benchmark source with dnceng;
do not change benchmark logic or product code.

Current-head run 33122720179 confirmed that the selected nightly packages
restore and the existing benchmark workflows run without changing benchmark
or product behavior.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>

4871.title: [4.151.x] Onboard Arcade infrastructure
4871.body:
[4.151.x] Onboard Arcade infrastructure (#4871)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4802
Follow-up: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4863

The release/4.151.x dnceng migration needs the Arcade and Darc bootstrap
already merged into main. Landing that bootstrap together with signing, BAR
publishing, package transport, and the other operational changes would make a
servicing change harder to review and roll back. Backport the behavior-neutral
layer first so the follow-up can build on a known infrastructure baseline.

Bring over the pinned Arcade 11.0.0-beta.26414.2 dependency metadata, complete
generated eng/common snapshot, isolated NoBuild restore graph, and engineering
cache inputs. Preserve the release branch's supported .NET 10.0.108 SDK and its
existing Cake build and pipeline entry points.

The generated eng/common tree and executable modes match the main change. The
only release-specific adaptation retains utils/Utils.sln because this branch
predates main's move to Utils.slnx. No public API, product, native, runtime,
signing, publishing, or transport behavior changes in this layer.

4832.title: [release] Move HarfBuzzSharp M151 to its revision bucket
4832.body:
[release] Move HarfBuzzSharp M151 to its revision bucket (#4832)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4833

M150 and M151 both carried native HarfBuzz 14.2.1 while independently
incrementing the same fourth version component. That allowed servicing releases
from separate Skia milestones to request identical HarfBuzzSharp package
versions.

Treat M150, which adopted 14.2.1, as the base 0-99 bucket and move the pending
M151 release from 14.2.1.3 to 14.2.1.103. Update the file version and the ten
HarfBuzzSharp package entries together while leaving the native release,
soname, assembly version, and SkiaSharp versions unchanged.

Record the adoption-relative rule beside the version entries: later milestones
on the same native X.Y.Z add 100, while an upgrade on main resets to zero and
establishes a new base. Older servicing lines remain on their existing native
HarfBuzz version.
